text:
devon: p99 jumped on a bunch of inference shards ~20:00 UTC, noticed a kernel switch around same time. possible noisy-host/driver combo.
yuki: saw this too, triage started from perf dashboards. p50 stable, p99 from ~45ms -> ~210ms for short seq (<=64).
maria: any recent rollout? driver or triton?
devon: infra pushed driver 525.85 yesterday + triton runtime picked a different autoselect path. logs show "kernel_selected=flash_attn_v3" for many small requests.
yuki: that kernel's mem footprint is higher for small batch sizes, causing KV cache evictions on these pods — evictions correlate with latency spikes. grep from agent log: ```[2026-11-07T19:59:12Z] model=redwood-gpt-small shard=shard-12 kernel_selected=flash_attn_v3 kv_cache_mem=2.4GB kv_evictions=12```.
aj: interesting — we saw a similar pattern but on larger seqs it was fine. so autoselect heuristic is favoring v3 for throughput but missing latency tradeoffs for short-seq workloads.
maria: can we force fallback to flash_attn_v2 on the affected pool to validate?
devon: yes. quick test: `rctl runtime set shard-12 --kernel flash_attn_v2` — after setting we saw p99 drop back to ~48ms in canary.
yuki: workaround looks good. root cause: heuristic drift in triton kernel selector after driver update (different occupancy numbers). Need to capture selector inputs for offline analysis.
aj: I'll add logs to capture: `selector_input: {batch_size, seq_len, sm_count, free_mem, active_kv_size}` and dump to s3 for last 48h.
sre-bot: deploy noted: rollback command applied to shard-12 by devon at 1809876600.
maria: next steps: 1) broaden rollback to other noisy shards as long as canary stays healthy, 2) produce regression PR to adjust autoselect threshold for seq_len<=128, 3) run microbench matrix (flash_attn_v2/v3 + driver 525/527) across sample traffic.
yuki: also add KV-cache occupancy metric to the per-shard dashboard (evictions/sec, kv_hit_ratio). helps catch thrash early.
devon: I'm concerned about noisy neighbor compounding: host-level cgroup pressure made page allocations slower which amplified kernel memory pressure. we'll schedule noisy-VM isolation for those hosts and mark for host remediation.
aj: assigning: I'll own the autoselect heuristic tweak (will open draft PR with test harness). Maria, can you own the cross-driver matrix and perf job?
maria: on it. I'll spin up perf rigs with driver 525/527 and run the benchmark matrix tomorrow.
yuki: for short-term alerting, change alert to fire if p99>120ms and kv_evictions>5 in 5m window.
devon: noted. Also capturing kernel-launch traces: snippet below where autoselect chose v3 even when expected v2: ```2026-11-07T19:58:59Z selector: batch=4 seq=32 sm=80 free_mem=3.1GB est_latency_v2=42 est_latency_v3=38 final_choice=v3```. est_latency numbers were misleading because they didn't include eviction cost.
aj: will modify selector to include an eviction penalty term derived from `active_kv_size / free_mem`. quick patch log in PR.
sre-bot: incident resolution checklist updated (incident-1809876543) with workaround and owner tags.
maria: final ask — can infra add a canary flag to disable triton_autoselect globally per-pool for emergency mitigation?
devon: yes, `TRITON_AUTOPICKER=off` per pool is feasible; infra can roll it out in 10-15m.
yuki: ok let's proceed with rollback + disable autoselect on noisy pool while we get PR and perf matrix done.
aj: I'll post PR link when ready.
maria: thanks team. closing loop after perf matrix and selector patch merge. :thumbsup:
